title: How Ruben Hassid built EasyGen and 120M LinkedIn views: content, founder branding and talking before building
summary: Ruben explains why he built EasyGen as a ghostwriter-style tool for his own team, and how founders should do personal branding by educating rather than sharing their life story. He also covers using employees' brands as a growth channel, LinkedIn micro-testing and language focus, and talking to people before building.

principles.text: Technical products lose without distribution; great founders invest in marketing and sharing early.
principles.quote: second time founder focus on marketing because they understand that if you build even the the best tool on the planet there's a high chance no one will care if you're not good enough at sharing it

principles.text: Personal branding means being relatable, not telling your life story; educate your audience instead.
principles.quote: you don't have to show about your life story to do that usually just educate me on that matter like tell me some of the learnings that you've discovered

principles.text: Make most of your content about the problem and journey your audience is in, not your product.
principles.quote: you can make your entire content 80% of your content about how hard it is to abandon a bad routine and how positive it is to embrace one good routine doesn't have to be about the the tool itself

principles.text: Turn employees into content channels with a small daily time investment and a simple, repeatable content workflow.
principles.quote: even if it's like 30 minutes to an hour a day that they invest in their brand it is positive to me it is positive to them

principles.text: Pick one language on LinkedIn because the algorithm micro-tests posts on small audiences and a mismatched audience scrolls away.
principles.quote: the best way is to focus on one language it's already hard enough and just double down on it

principles.text: Talk about the solution to real people before and while you build, and stay obsessed with the people you help, not the product.
principles.quote: before starting to build something as fast as possible talk about the solution as fast as possible to other people that's the best way to start
